nodes.title: Linear SHM & Differential Equation
points: Periodic motion repeats at equal intervals of time. Oscillatory motion is to-and-fro periodic motion about a mean position.
Linear Simple Harmonic Motion (SHM): Restoring force is directly proportional to displacement from mean position and oppositely directed: F = −kx.
Differential equation of linear SHM: d²x/dt² + ω²x = 0, where ω² = k/m.
Angular frequency: ω = √(k/m). Time period T = 2π/ω = 2π√(m/k). Frequency n = 1/T = (1/2π)√(k/m).
Force constant k = mω² (SI unit: N/m, dimensions [M¹L⁰T⁻²]).

nodes.title: Kinematics of Linear SHM
points: Acceleration: a = −ω²x. It is maximum at extreme positions (a_max = ω²A) and zero at mean position (x = 0).
Velocity: v = ±ω√(A² − x²). It is maximum at mean position (v_max = ωA) and zero at extreme positions (x = ±A).
Displacement starting from mean position: x = A sin(ωt).
Displacement starting from positive extreme position: x = A cos(ωt).
General displacement: x = A sin(ωt + α), where α is initial phase (epoch).

nodes.title: Phase, Epoch & Phase Relations
points: Phase (θ = ωt + α) describes the instantaneous state of motion (magnitude and direction of displacement).
Epoch α is the phase at t = 0 (initial phase).
Phase difference between displacement and velocity is π/2 rad (90°): Velocity leads displacement by π/2.
Phase difference between velocity and acceleration is π/2 rad (90°): Acceleration leads velocity by π/2.
Phase difference between displacement and acceleration is π rad (180°): Acceleration is in opposite phase to displacement.

nodes.title: Energy in SHM & Conservation
points: Potential Energy: PE = ½ kx² = ½ mω²x² = ½ mω²A² sin²(ωt + α). PE is minimum (0) at mean position and maximum (½ kA²) at extremes.
Kinetic Energy: KE = ½ mv² = ½ k(A² − x²) = ½ mω²A² cos²(ωt + α). KE is maximum (½ kA²) at mean position and zero at extremes.
Total Energy: TE = KE + PE = ½ kA² = ½ mω²A² = 2π² m n² A² = constant (conserved throughout).
Total energy is directly proportional to mass (m), square of amplitude (A²), and square of frequency (n²).
At x = ±A/√2: KE = PE = ½ TE. Average KE over one period = ¼ kA²; Average PE = ¼ kA².

nodes.title: Simple Pendulum & Laws
points: An ideal simple pendulum consists of a heavy point mass suspended by a weightless, inextensible, perfectly flexible string.
Restoring torque: τ = −(mg sinθ)L ≈ −mgLθ (for small angular amplitude θ < 10°).
Time period: T = 2π√(L/g). Frequency n = (1/2π)√(g/L).
Laws of simple pendulum: Law of length (T ∝ √L), Law of gravity (T ∝ 1/√g), Law of mass (independent of mass), Law of isochronism (independent of amplitude for small θ).
Seconds pendulum: A pendulum whose period is exactly 2 seconds (T = 2 s). Length on Earth L ≈ 0.993 m ≈ 1 m.

formulas.label: Seconds pendulum length
formulas.expr: L = g / π² ≈ 1 m (for T = 2 s)

nodes.title: Angular SHM & Magnet in B-Field
points: Angular SHM: Oscillatory motion where restoring torque is directly proportional to angular displacement: τ = −cθ.
Differential equation of angular SHM: I d²θ/dt² + cθ = 0, where I is moment of inertia and c is restoring torque per unit twist.
Period of angular SHM: T = 2π√(I/c).
Bar magnet vibrating in uniform magnetic field B: Restoring torque τ = −MB sinθ ≈ −MBθ.
Time period of vibrating magnet: T = 2π√(I / MB), where M is magnetic dipole moment and B is magnetic induction.

nodes.title: Composition of Two SHMs
points: Superposition of two SHMs of same period along the same straight line: x₁ = A₁ sin(ωt + α₁), x₂ = A₂ sin(ωt + α₂).
Resultant motion is also an SHM of the same period: R sin(ωt + δ).
Resultant amplitude: R = √(A₁² + A₂² + 2A₁A₂ cos(α₁ − α₂)).
Initial phase of resultant: tanδ = (A₁ sinα₁ + A₂ sinα₂) / (A₁ cosα₁ + A₂ cosα₂).
Special Cases: (1) If phase difference Δα = 0, R = A₁ + A₂; (2) If Δα = π, R = |A₁ − A₂|; (3) If Δα = π/2 and A₁ = A₂, R = A√2.

formulas.label: Resultant phase
formulas.expr: tanδ = (A₁ sinα₁ + A₂ sinα₂) / (A₁ cosα₁ + A₂ cosα₂)

nodes.title: Damped, Free & Forced Oscillations, Resonance
points: Free oscillations: System oscillates with its natural frequency when displaced and released, with no external force.
Damped oscillations: Oscillations whose amplitude decreases exponentially with time due to dissipative forces (friction, viscosity).
Damping force: F_d = −b v = −b(dx/dt), where b is damping constant.
Damped amplitude: A(t) = A₀ e^(−bt / 2m). Mechanical energy is dissipated as heat.
Forced oscillations: Oscillations under an external periodic driving force F = F₀ sin(ω_d t).
Resonance: When driving frequency equals natural frequency (ω_d = ω₀), amplitude of oscillation becomes maximum.

nodes.title: Must-Know Board Derivations & Graph Essentials
points: Board Favourite #1: Derive differential equation of linear SHM and obtain expressions for acceleration, velocity, and displacement.
Board Favourite #2: Show that total energy in linear SHM is conserved at all positions and proportional to A² and n².
Board Favourite #3: Derive expression for the period of a simple pendulum T = 2π√(L/g) and state its laws.
Board Favourite #4: Derive expression for resultant amplitude of composition of two parallel SHMs.
Graphs to Master: (1) x, v, a vs time graphs showing phase shifts; (2) KE and PE vs displacement parabola showing TE = constant.

nodes.title: MHT-CET Shortcuts, Spring Hacks & Speed Tricks
points: Spring Combinations: Series ⟹ 1/k_s = 1/k₁ + 1/k₂ (so T = 2π√[m(k₁+k₂)/(k₁k₂)]); Parallel ⟹ k_p = k₁ + k₂ (so T = 2π√[m/(k₁+k₂)]).
Cutting a Spring: When a spring of constant k is cut into n equal parts, each part has spring constant k' = n k (stiffer).
Special Positions of Energy: (1) KE = PE at x = A/√2; (2) KE = 3 PE at x = A/2; (3) PE = 3 KE at x = A√3/2.
Time Taken Shortcuts: Time to travel from mean to A/2 is t = T/12; Time to travel from A/2 to extreme A is t = T/6.
Relation between v_max and a_max: a_max / v_max = ω; v_max² / a_max = A.
Effective g in Elevator: Accelerating up ⟹ g_eff = g + a (T decreases); Accelerating down ⟹ g_eff = g − a (T increases); Free fall ⟹ g_eff = 0 (T = ∞, pendulum stops).
